_comment: Curated voice catalogue. Each entry maps a stable 'id' to a Piper voice model. Ids are a durable contract - the APU stores the selected id in its settings table - so never rename one after release; add a new entry instead. To add a voice: copy an entry, set a unique id, fill model/config/model_url/config_url from https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices, then run `syscon-tts download-voices <id>`. A site that does not want to edit this file can point SYSCON_TTS_EXTRA_MANIFEST at its own JSON (same shape) to add or replace entries, or simply drop the .onnx and .onnx.json into the voices directory, where they are discovered automatically.
_integrity: Download URLs are pinned to one commit of rhasspy/piper-voices rather than 'main', so an upstream re-upload cannot change how a voice id sounds on newly provisioned sites. model_sha256/config_sha256 are verified after every download and by `syscon-tts doctor`; a mismatch is refused. To move to a newer upload, change the commit in both URLs and update both hashes in the same release.
_licensing: PlantStar ships to paying customers, so this catalogue only includes voices whose model card states a license permitting commercial use (public domain, CC0, Unlicense, CC BY). 'license' records the DATASET license from the upstream MODEL_CARD; a voice is reported by `syscon-tts doctor` as needing review (and skipped by a bulk `download-voices`) when that license is non-permissive OR when 'license_review_required' is set true. The override exists because a Piper voice is often fine-tuned from another checkpoint, and that base can carry a restriction a permissive dataset license does not clear; 'lineage' records the provenance. FIVE catalogued voices (es_mx_ald, es_es_davefx, fr_fr_siwis, de_de_thorsten, zh_cn_huayan) are held on exactly this ground -- they are fine-tuned from research-only en_US-lessac -- so Spanish, French, German and Chinese have no cleared native voice until legal signs off; see _review_lessac. Voices deliberately NOT catalogued: en_US-ryan, en_US-hfc_female, en_US-hfc_male and zh_CN-xiao_ya (CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial); en_US-amy, en_GB-alan and en_US-lessac (license stated only as 'see dataset URL', unverified); zh_CN-chaowen (CC0 dataset but finetuned from the non-commercial xiao_ya). Any of them can still be used by a site that has cleared it - see DEPLOY.md.
_review_lessac: NOTE FOR FUTURE REVIEWERS -- the en_US-lessac lineage family. Five catalogued voices are fine-tuned (directly or transitively) from en_US-lessac, whose Blizzard 2013 training data is research-only and excludes commercial voice-synthesis products: es_mx_ald, es_es_davefx, fr_fr_siwis, de_de_thorsten and zh_cn_huayan. Each was verified against its MODEL_CARD at the pinned commit (c10ece1aade47bb51c153c893d14e5bf8e5b7117). The DATASET license of each is permissive (Unlicense/CC0/CC BY 4.0) or, for huayan, Unknown -- but the MODEL lineage is the concern, so all five carry license_review_required: true and are held: doctor flags them and bulk download-voices skips them. CONSEQUENCE: Spanish, French, German and Chinese sites have no cleared native voice in this catalogue. Only Spanish has a cleared interim stand-in (es_es_carlfm, trained from scratch); fr/de/zh have none, so those sites fall back to the default English voice until this clears. TO CLEAR THE FAMILY once legal signs off on the lessac lineage: set 'license_review_required' to false on es_mx_ald, es_es_davefx, fr_fr_siwis and de_de_thorsten. huayan is NOT cleared by that step alone -- its Unknown dataset license is a separate hold that also needs sign-off (and its 'license' field updated from 'unknown'). The clean long-term fix for any locale is to retrain on its own permissive dataset from a clean base; see _review_es_mx for the Spanish plan.
_review_es_mx: NOTE FOR FUTURE REVIEWERS -- Mexican Spanish voice selection. Both Piper es_MX voices trace to research-only en_US-lessac (es_mx_ald -> davefx -> lessac; the other, es_MX-claude, has an undocumented base and a non-commercial sibling, so it is not catalogued). Until legal clears the lessac lineage, es_mx_ald is held (license_review_required: true) and the CLEARED es_es_carlfm (Castilian, trained from scratch, public domain) stands in for Mexican Spanish. Deployments set this via SYSCON_TTS_DEFAULT_VOICES=es_MX=es_es_carlfm (or default_voices={'es_MX': 'es_es_carlfm'} in code). TO SWITCH BACK ONCE legal signs off on es_mx_ald: (1) set 'license_review_required' to false on the es_mx_ald entry here (that alone makes doctor and bulk download-voices treat it as cleared again); (2) change the es_MX default mapping from es_es_carlfm to es_mx_ald. That is the whole switch; nothing else references the interim choice. The genuinely clean long-term option is to RETRAIN on the Ald Mexican dataset (already public domain) from a clean base such as es_es_carlfm or from scratch, which keeps the Mexican accent without the lessac lineage.
_quality: x_low (smallest/fastest) < low < medium (balanced; the APU default) < high (largest/slowest). Medium models are roughly 60 MB on disk and in RSS.

voices.name: Ald - Mexican Spanish
voices.lineage: Fine-tuned from es_ES-davefx, which is fine-tuned from en_US-lessac. Lessac's Blizzard 2013 data is research-only and excludes commercial voice-synthesis products, so this model's lineage may not clear for a product we sell, even though the Ald dataset itself is public domain.
voices.notes: HELD FOR LICENSE REVIEW (model lineage, not the dataset). The native Mexican voice; use once legal clears the lessac lineage. Interim cleared substitute for es_MX is es_es_carlfm. See _review_es_mx and DEPLOY.md 'Choosing the voice'.

voices.name: DaveFX - Spanish (Spain), male
voices.lineage: Fine-tuned from en_US-lessac (Blizzard 2013, research-only, excludes commercial voice-synthesis products), per the model card at the pinned commit. The CC0 dataset does not clear the model lineage.
voices.notes: HELD FOR LICENSE REVIEW (model lineage, not the dataset). Shares the lessac lineage flagged on es_mx_ald. es_es_carlfm is the cleared Castilian alternative.

voices.name: CarlFM - Spanish (Spain), male
voices.lineage: Trained from scratch (no en_US-lessac lineage), per the model card. Dataset is public domain.
voices.notes: Cleared for commercial use: clean lineage and a public-domain dataset. Castilian (Spain) accent and x_low quality (16 kHz), so it is the INTERIM substitute for Mexican Spanish while es_mx_ald is under license review -- intelligible, not native. Map it in with SYSCON_TTS_DEFAULT_VOICES=es_MX=es_es_carlfm. See _review_es_mx.

voices.name: Huayan - Mandarin Chinese
voices.lineage: Fine-tuned from en_US-lessac (Blizzard 2013, research-only, excludes commercial voice-synthesis products), per the model card at the pinned commit. Held on two independent grounds: this lessac lineage AND a dataset license the model card states as 'Unknown'.
voices.notes: HELD FOR LICENSE REVIEW on two grounds: an 'Unknown' dataset license (already non-permissive) AND the lessac model lineage (see _review_lessac). Clearing the lessac family alone does NOT clear this voice -- the Unknown dataset license still needs sign-off. The only Mandarin voice Piper 1.2 can run whose dataset license is not explicitly non-commercial; serves both zh-Hans and zh-Hant sites (same spoken language, only the script differs). Spot-check Traditional text before promising it.

voices.name: Siwis - French, female
voices.lineage: Fine-tuned from en_US-lessac (Blizzard 2013, research-only, excludes commercial voice-synthesis products), per the model card at the pinned commit. The CC BY 4.0 dataset does not clear the model lineage.
voices.notes: HELD FOR LICENSE REVIEW (model lineage, not the dataset). Part of the lessac-lineage family; see _review_lessac. CC BY 4.0 would otherwise permit commercial use with attribution (credit the SIWIS corpus wherever the product credits third-party components) -- but the model is finetuned from lessac. There is no cleared French substitute in this catalogue, so a French site stays on the default voice until legal clears the lessac family or a clean fr voice is added.
